crosswalks.label: Information Security Analysts
crosswalks.rationale: The occupation covers security assessment/risk mitigation but also network, access, incident and general security work beyond application security.

crosswalks.label: Software Security Assessment
crosswalks.rationale: This current NICE Work Role directly covers analyzing application/software security and delivering actionable results, but NICE explicitly says a Work Role is not synonymous with a job or occupation.

crosswalks.label: Application Security Verification Standard 5.0.0
crosswalks.rationale: ASVS supplies application-security verification requirements, not an occupation definition; it is one domain layer inside the profession.

findings.summary: A broad security occupation and a software-security assessment Work Role describe different layers of the human work; NICE explicitly warns that Work Roles are not jobs or occupations.
findings.rationale: The current package is narrower than Information Security Analyst and already focuses on application threat/review/verification, so preserving multiple concept layers prevents scope inflation.

findings.summary: NICE Software Security Assessment and ASVS strongly support application/security analysis, verification requirements and actionable remediation evidence.
findings.rationale: Threat modeling, requirement mapping, secure review, authorized defensive verification and remediation validation are already core body machinery.

findings.summary: NICE 2.2.0 updated DevSecOps competency content and added a Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management Work Role, showing adjacent work that may intersect application security without belonging wholly inside it.
findings.rationale: The body mentions software supply-chain/dependency security, but should distinguish application-owned dependency verification from organizational C-SCRM and DevSecOps responsibilities.

findings.summary: O*NET Information Security Analyst includes firewall, virus monitoring, user training, access administration and breach-response tasks that are not Application Security ownership by default.
findings.rationale: Bulk-importing the broader occupation would erase the package's explicit network/identity/incident boundaries.

gaps_against_body.description: Add a domain-work-role crosswalk showing which NICE Work Roles/Competency Areas are core, adjacent or excluded so application security can compose with Secure Software Development, DevSecOps, C-SCRM and incident roles without absorbing them.

Deepen the boundary between application dependency verification and organizational cybersecurity supply-chain risk management; add explicit handoff when risk exceeds application-owned dependency evidence.

nonclaims: This research does not authorize penetration testing, production testing, access to systems/data, risk acceptance or legal compliance claims.
A NICE Work Role is not treated as a whole occupation or job.
ASVS is a verification standard layer and does not by itself prove professional competence or application security.

high_stakes.authorization_nonclaim: Research and package capability do not grant security-testing authorization, risk acceptance, access rights, or legal/compliance authority; all execution remains bounded by explicit target/action scope.
